designNotes: Pure white field with a 1120px live area on an 80px margin and a 24px baseline grid, shown as faint hairlines. The headline is set left-aligned in Helvetica Bold at 92/96 so every line sits on the baseline grid, with a strong size jump down to the 14px captions. The illustration is asymmetric and placed in the right columns: one red point (the only accent, repeated in the headline's full stop and the '1 → n' label) sends orthogonal black links out to square and ring nodes, all snapped to shared column and baseline coordinates. Three caption columns under a hairline rule lay out the reading order: idea, connection, system. Most of the canvas is left as negative space.

A mostly white Bauhaus poster on a 120 px grid where a red ring (the idea) feeds black orthogonal rules into a yellow square, a rotated diamond, a blue triangle and a red half-disc, with the center and corners left as #FFFFFF so the background reads correctly.
Constructivist study: a halftone bulb cutout rides a -12° diagonal into a hub, a red band slashes in, spokes connect four nodes.

Open white field holding a few pure, flat forms with no texture. A lone red circle in the upper left is the idea; one thin black line leads it down into a tilted cluster: a black rectangle, a long yellow bar, a blue square, a red bar and a black cross, joined by hairlines into a balanced system. The whole cluster is rotated -16° so it reads as floating weight. The headline is small and set at an angle along the forms, so negative space and relative scale carry the meaning. Uses only black, white and the three primary tokens.

A strict De Stijl grid where heavy black horizontal and vertical rules cut white into cells; small red, blue and yellow fields sit at the edges, square nodes mark each junction, and the large white central cell holds flush-left type, so #FFFFFF stays the main field.

Symmetrical Art Deco on black, ivory and restrained gold. A sunburst clipped inside a double-lined arch fans out from the horizon behind a stepped ziggurat with ivory fluting. At the apex a gilded disc (the idea) sends symmetrical ivory lines through diamond nodes down to the tower's steps, turning the idea into an ordered system. The only gold effect is one narrow diagonal highlight sweep on the disc and tower outline. Stepped corner brackets, side pylons, a chevron band and widely spaced geometric caps give a precise, monumental type hierarchy.
A seed-idea sprouts vines, then blooms, and one tendril links them into a connected system inside a night-garden Art Nouveau frame.

Swiss/International layout on a 12-column hairline grid with a 80px margin. Reading order goes top to bottom: label bar, two-line Helvetica headline, a short blue rule, then a three-stage diagram read left to right (point → link → network) with numbered captions in shared columns underneath. Only three inks; blue marks just the idea node and the word 'system.' Hierarchy comes from size and placement, not decoration.
Dusk-slate mid-century poster: a figure raises a bright idea that draws out into a connected system of nodes.
An idea sticker spawns a linked Memphis network on a deep-indigo halftone field with ring pulse and confetti.
Pop Art comic page: a bulb lights its halftone halo, BING!, ZAP!, and three wired bulbs form a connected system.

A monochrome Op Art study: one reused set of concentric rings is split and offset at its middle so it vibrates against itself, beside bands of stripes, checks and skewed stripes, while the type sits in the calm white top-left zone and most of the page stays #FFFFFF.
A single pastel-on-violet vortex spirals from one cream spark into orbiting nodes, while ordered saturated waves flow below a calm, readable title zone.
A floating porcelain egg opens to show its own sun and cloud, which tether out satellites into a connected system under dusk light.
Raw browser chrome, a hard lime highlight bar and hatched terminal block pair a huge IDEA = SYSTEM headline with orthogonally wired window nodes, all in a clear numbered order.
Ransom-note headline, torn paper and a Rough.js ink network pasted onto cool grey graph paper; the CONNECTED stamp is the punchline.
Distressed IDEA ink surfaces, a rough dashed network wires out from a rust dot, and a torn SYSTEM paste-up lands on cold xerox stock.
One green point runs along a single hairline into a four-node diamond, with wide warm negative space, matching 1.5px strokes and one light sans line held to a strict left margin.

Opus-authored backstage motion preview: the canonical storyboard crew keep consistent cutout silhouettes and role props, with staggered delivery, lettering, lighting, sound and camera tasks around a readable presentation board.

A four-panel Manga idea sequence with repaired perspective-aware eye openings, coordinated gaze, matching lid masks and simplified iris details. This character example illustrates conditional eye-construction guidance; Manga subjects remain driven by the brief.

Claude Opus 5.5 code-drawn Cassette Futurism console: beige cases with screws and embossed labels around charcoal/olive panels, a green-phosphor CRT with scanlines, glow, vignette and seeded noise, a tape transport with stepping reels and amber counter, toggles, a detented knob, square keys and a warning-only red master-caution lamp. The composition types a boot log, cuts through channel static to a NAV page and steps every action at 12fps from absolute time.

Claude Opus 5.5 code-drawn Terminal Lyric Duotone Anime study: an original, clearly illustrative headphone bust in flat ultramarine, cream and near-black inside a CRT terminal frame with scanlines, seeded grain, vignette and corner brackets; a decoding §07 header, a bilingual monospace/CJK caption with a growing progress underline and signal-blue keyword, a HUD detection box and specimen card that build from authored data, a keyword title that settles from an RGB offset into a thin ellipse ring, and one warning-only red label. Not reference artwork, footage or lyrics.

Generalised from the observed visual grammar (clustered circular hubs, curved fine-particle streams carrying transfer, restrained halos and semantic state accents, sparse dotted field, compact technical labels, fixed layout while flow and emphasis change) into a domain-neutral node-link style. No source labels, product names, layout, data or code are reused. Motion is defined as five scripted beats (activation, transfer, arrival, settle, overview) evaluated deterministically from composition time, with seeded particles bound to authored source-to-destination curves. The palette is role-based and illustrative with a scene-dependent background; Dark and Light variants share the same roles, and contrast figures are hand-computed WCAG approximations to recheck with chroma-js on composited frames. Motion references are limited to optional motion-030 and motion-016; combinations are limited to style-097 and style-098. The card SVG shows 10 nodes in three clusters around a primary hub, dotted round-cap strokes simulating particle streams that densify toward destinations, warm halos on the active path, one dashed fault ring, a faint dot field and vignette, and three generic labels: INTAKE, EXCHANGE, OUTCOME.

Claude Opus 5.5 code-drawn Vintage Rubber Hose Animation sample. An original crooked house on a hill at night shows the hand-inked style: strong irregular ink silhouettes, painterly sepia rim light and dry-brush shadow, small glowing windows, leaning bare trees, layered painterly sky and wind streaks. The house squashes, stretches and settles in elastic drawings that change 12 times a second. It then cuts to the optional film-leader countdown, 3, 2, 1: precise concentric rings and crosshairs, a large pale sans-serif numeral and a darker rotating clock-wipe sector on a photographic plate with grain, scratches, dust and gate weave. The house and sequence are sample content, not requirements.
